---
title: "Glossary"
description: "Plain-language definitions of the statistical terms used on this site."
toc: false
---

Terms with a dotted underline on any page link here. Hover over one to read its definition without leaving the page.

[At risk]{#at-risk}
:   Still being followed, and not yet having had the event, at a given moment.

[Ceiling (or floor) effect]{#ceiling-effect}
:   Many patients score the best (or worst) value a scale allows, so the scale cannot show how much better (or worse) they really are.

[Censored]{#censored}
:   Followed for a while without having the event, then no longer observed: the study ended, the patient moved away, or the patient died. All we know is that the event had not happened by then.

[Confidence interval (CI)]{#confidence-interval}
:   A range of values for the true effect that fit the data. A 95% CI comes from a method that captures the true value in 95 of 100 repeated studies.

[Degrees of freedom (df)]{#degrees-of-freedom}
:   Roughly, the number of independent pieces of information left for estimating the noise: the sample size minus the number of quantities already estimated. Software uses it to pick the reference distribution for a test statistic.

[Effect size]{#effect-size}
:   A number that says how large a difference or an association is. The p-value doesn't say that.

[Expected count]{#expected-count}
:   The count a table cell would hold if the outcome had nothing to do with the group: row total × column total ÷ grand total.

[Hazard ratio (HR)]{#hazard-ratio}
:   One group's hazard divided by the other's. The hazard is the moment-to-moment risk of the event among those still at risk, so a hazard ratio of 2 means the event is twice as likely at any moment.

[Interquartile range (IQR)]{#iqr}
:   The range that holds the middle half of the values, from the 25th percentile to the 75th.

[Mean]{#mean}
:   The average: add up the values and divide by how many there are.

[Median]{#median}
:   The middle value when the values are sorted: half lie below it and half above.

[Null hypothesis]{#null-hypothesis}
:   The assumption a test starts from: that there is no difference or no association. The p-value is calculated as if it were true.

[Odds ratio]{#odds-ratio}
:   The odds of the outcome in one group divided by the odds in the other. The odds are the number with the outcome divided by the number without it.

[p-value]{#p-value}
:   The probability of a result at least as extreme as yours if there were truly no difference. A small p-value means the data would be surprising if there were no difference. It is not the probability that there is no difference.

[Paired]{#paired}
:   Two measurements that belong together: the same patient before and after surgery, or the left and right hip of one person.

[Percentile]{#percentile}
:   The value below which a given percentage of the values lie. A quarter of the values lie below the 25th percentile.

[Rank]{#rank}
:   A value's position when all the values are sorted from lowest to highest. Tied values share the average of their positions.

[Scientific notation]{#scientific-notation}
:   How software prints very small or very large numbers. 2.7e-08 means 2.7 with the decimal point moved 8 places to the left: 0.000000027.

[Skewed]{#skewed}
:   Lopsided: most values sit at one end and a long tail stretches out to the other.

[Standard deviation (SD)]{#standard-deviation}
:   The typical distance of a value from the mean. A small SD means the values sit close together.

[Standard error]{#standard-error}
:   How much an estimate, such as a mean or a difference between two means, would vary from one sample to the next. It shrinks as the sample grows. It is not the SD, which describes how spread out the patients are.

[Test statistic]{#test-statistic}
:   A single number, such as t, U or χ², that a test calculates from the data to measure how far they are from "no difference".

[Variance]{#variance}
:   The standard deviation squared. Tests such as ANOVA compare variances because they can be added up.

[Wald confidence interval]{#wald-interval}
:   The simplest kind of CI: the estimate plus and minus about 2 standard errors (1.96 for a 95% CI).
